title: LowDiff: Efficient Frequent Checkpointing via Low-Cost Differential for High-Performance Distributed Training Systems
problem: Frequent checkpointing for fast failure recovery in distributed deep learning training generates numerous checkpoints, incurring substantial storage costs and degrading training performance.
motivation: Distributed training fails frequently; checkpointing enables recovery but adds significant overhead. Differential checkpointing reduces costs but has only been applied to recommendation systems, not general training.
method: LowDiff reuses compressed gradients (already computed in distributed training) as differential checkpoints to reduce storage costs. Includes batched gradient write optimization and dynamic tuning of checkpoint frequency and batching size.
key_novelty: Novel reuse of gradient compression (common in distributed training) as a differential checkpoint mechanism with dynamic tuning for optimal performance.
contributions: Enables checkpointing frequency up to per-iteration with less than 3.1% training time overhead
Reuses existing gradient compression infrastructure for differential checkpoints
Batched gradient write optimization for efficient persistence
Dynamic tuning of checkpoint frequency and batch size
workloads: Large distributed deep learning model training
limitations: Full-text not available; specific workload details and model types not provided. Scalability characteristics not detailed.
